title: CartoDB API Key Problems
rationale: Facts: reporter RightChain says the CartoDB basemap watermark persists despite generating and correctly retrieving a valid CartoDB API key and passing it via addProviderTiles('CartoDB.Positron', options=providerTileOptions(key=...)); the same key mechanism works for ThunderForest via key/apikey. A contributor (jack-davison) independently confirms the same watermark shows on the project's own pkgdown 'basemaps' article for CartoDB tiles. The reporter then contacted CartoDB support, who diagnosed that the CartoDB provider template omits the 'key' parameter, so addProviderTiles() silently drops it; the reporter confirms a workaround using addTiles() with a hand-built tile URL plus a manually appended '?key=' query parameter removes the watermark. Classification hypothesis: bug -- a missing 'key' URL parameter in leaflet's built-in CartoDB provider template definition, not a feature request or usage error. Duplicate check: searched open/closed issues for 'CartoDB key'; no other issue found besides this one. Wrong-location check: correct repo -- rstudio/leaflet owns the addProviderTiles()/provider template data that is missing the parameter. Regression check: not applicable -- no evidence the CartoDB provider ever included the key parameter in an older release; the template appears to have never supported it. Reproduction plan: the reporter's addProviderTiles() snippet plus screenshot reproduces the watermark; the CartoDB-support-confirmed addTiles() workaround (building the tile URL and appending ?key=<value>) is a directly runnable, comparison-based repro of the fix. Impact: moderate -- affects any app using addProviderTiles() with CartoDB basemaps and a valid API key (increasingly required as CartoDB enforces key usage), and is independently confirmed visible on the package's own public documentation site. Priority: Medium -- valid, well-diagnosed bug with a documented workaround. Recommended next action: label Priority: Medium and mark ai-triage:done; two independent reporters plus a CartoDB-support-confirmed root cause make this safe to label without further review.

title: Bookmark file-input restore leaks a TemporaryDirectory when a session never ends
rationale: Facts: maintainer schloerke self-filed this, noting that shiny/input_handler.py's bookmark file-input restore path creates a tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() and only cleans it up via session.on_ended(); if a session object is built and never explicitly ended (as in some unit tests), the directory is only reclaimed at garbage-collection time, emitting ResourceWarning: Implicitly cleaning up .... The report explains this became visible after PR #2480 turned on filterwarnings=error, was misattributed to an unrelated test by pytest, and is currently masked by a blanket ResourceWarning ignore in pytest.ini; it also notes shiny/ui/_theme.py has the same GC-cleanup pattern as a second, intentional source. Three options (leave as-is, fix the test harness, or clean up deterministically) are proposed without a final decision. Classification hypothesis: bug -- a real resource-lifecycle leak in a real-session edge case (session that never ends), currently masked rather than fixed, though the author frames it primarily as a decision to record. Duplicate check: no other open issue on this TemporaryDirectory/ResourceWarning leak found. Wrong-location check: correct repo -- shiny/input_handler.py is core py-shiny code. Regression check: not applicable -- no prior-version comparison; this is an existing code path newly exposed by stricter test warnings. Reproduction plan: the maintainer's own description (build a Session, exercise the bookmark file-input restore path, never call the on_ended callback, then force garbage collection) is a concrete, minimal repro; the referenced pytest.ini ignore and PR #2480 corroborate it. Impact: low -- the author explicitly assesses this as a test-environment artifact with no effect on real running apps, since real sessions do end and trigger the cleanup callback. Priority: Low. Recommended next action: label Priority: Low and mark ai-triage:done; maintainer-authored, low-risk, and explicitly scoped as low impact, safe to label without further review.

rationale: Facts: maintainer schloerke self-filed this tracking issue for removing Pyright now that Pyrefly is the primary type checker; it documents every remaining Pyright touchpoint (config, Makefile stub-generation targets, CI job, 1463 # pyright: ignore comments) and investigates the first of two blockers -- pyrefly stubgen's stub generation for folium/uvicorn/seaborn -- finding two upstream stubgen bugs (dropped __all__, dropped private symbols referenced by public aliases) fixed only in an unreleased pyrefly 1.2.0.dev. Comments show a contributor (ChidiebereNjoku) already picked up the scoped migration once pyrefly 1.2.0 went stable and opened PR #2478, now awaiting maintainer review; a second blocker (validating shinylive's typings under Pyrefly) is explicitly marked not yet investigated. Classification hypothesis: none of the rubric's special categories -- a maintainer-owned engineering/chore tracking issue with active, in-progress work. Duplicate check: not applicable -- a unique tracking issue for this specific migration. Wrong-location check: correct repo -- internal py-shiny tooling/CI concern. Regression check: not applicable. Reproduction plan: not applicable -- the issue documents the verification matrix (pyrefly vs pyright output across three stub-generation configurations) that was already run. Impact: low -- internal developer-tooling migration with no end-user-facing effect; work is already in progress via PR #2478. Priority: Low. Recommended next action: label Priority: Low and mark ai-triage:done; maintainer-authored chore with active follow-through, safe to label without further review.

title: No easy way to reuse an uploaded file from its id
rationale: Facts: maintainer thisisnic self-filed this (crediting an AI-generated summary) noting that reusing a previously uploaded file requires manually rebuilding a ContentUploaded from chat.files.get() metadata, and that this fails for OpenAI specifically because file_get() returns mime_type=None while ContentUploaded.mime_type is a required str, forcing callers to guess the MIME type from the filename; cites ellmer's just-merged fix (tidyverse/ellmer#1116, #1119), which has chat$file_get() return a ready-to-use ContentUploaded with metadata on extra and a filename-based MIME guess, and suggests chatlas either mirror that or add a FileMetadata.to_content() helper. Classification hypothesis: feature -- an API-ergonomics gap (missing helper/parity with a just-shipped ellmer fix), not a bug in existing documented behavior. Duplicate check: no other open issue on file-reuse/ContentUploaded ergonomics found. Wrong-location check: correct repo -- chatlas' own file-handling API. Regression check: not applicable -- this functionality was never fully ergonomic; no prior-release comparison given. Reproduction plan: not applicable to a feature request; the issue includes the exact failing manual-reconstruction code path for OpenAI as illustration. Impact: low -- a workflow inconvenience with a documented (if clunky) manual workaround for two of three providers, and a guessing workaround for OpenAI. Priority: Low. Recommended next action: label Priority: Low and mark ai-triage:done; maintainer-authored, well-scoped parity request, safe to label without further review.

title: Anthropic provider drops empty assistant turns, breaking role alternation
rationale: Facts: maintainer cpsievert self-filed this, showing that AnthropicProvider._as_message_params drops assistant turns with zero content blocks via a continue statement instead of substituting a placeholder, which can produce two consecutive user-role messages and violate Anthropic's strict user/assistant alternation requirement; includes a standalone repro script demonstrating the drop and the resulting ['user','user'] role sequence, references ellmer's just-merged equivalent fix (tidyverse/ellmer#1099/#1100, following #711/#1070) which sends a '[empty string]' placeholder instead of dropping the turn, and explicitly flags as an open question whether chatlas's real Anthropic response-parsing path can ever actually produce an AssistantTurn with contents=[] in practice. Classification hypothesis: bug -- a demonstrably unsafe code path in message construction, though the author notes uncertainty about how often (if ever) it is reached via normal API responses today. Duplicate check: found closed #10 ('all messages must have non-empty content...') which addressed a related but distinct empty-content scenario; no open duplicate. Wrong-location check: correct repo -- chatlas/_provider_anthropic.py. Regression check: not applicable -- this is a latent bug being proactively fixed to match ellmer, not a behavior change from an older chatlas release. Reproduction plan: the included standalone script (constructing turns with an empty-content AssistantTurn and calling _as_message_params directly) is directly runnable and already demonstrates the invalid role sequence. Impact: uncertain but potentially significant if triggered -- code that would otherwise be unsafe if such a turn is ever constructed today or in the future. Priority: Medium -- reflects the uncertainty over real-world trigger frequency, balanced against a demonstrably unsafe code path with a clear, low-risk fix mirroring an already-shipped ellmer change. Recommended next action: label Priority: Medium and mark ai-triage:done; maintainer-authored with a precise repro and a well-specified fix, safe to label without further review.

title: Bedrock providers ignore AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_BEDROCK_RUNTIME env var
rationale: Facts: maintainer cpsievert self-filed this, showing that both Bedrock provider implementations (_provider_bedrock.py, _provider_bedrock_converse.py) always compute base_url from the AWS region formula when no explicit base_url is passed, bypassing botocore's standard AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_BEDROCK_RUNTIME (and generic AWS_ENDPOINT_URL) env-var convention used for custom Bedrock endpoints (VPC endpoints, proxies, local testing, FIPS); cites ellmer's just-merged equivalent fix (tidyverse/ellmer#1104) and notes the analogous ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL case is already handled for free via the underlying anthropic SDK. Classification hypothesis: bug/feature-parity -- a missing standard-env-var fallback, not a behavior regression. Duplicate check: searched 'Bedrock'; found #410 and #411 which are other, distinct Bedrock-mantle bugs (URL content sources, default model/prefix), not duplicates of this env-var gap. Wrong-location check: correct repo -- chatlas/_provider_bedrock*.py. Regression check: not applicable -- this behavior was never implemented, not lost. Reproduction plan: not included as a runnable repro, but the fix is precisely located (two resolved_base_url = base_url or bedrock_base_url(...) call sites) and mirrors an already-merged upstream ellmer change. Impact: low -- affects only users targeting custom Bedrock runtime endpoints, who have a full workaround today (pass base_url explicitly). Priority: Low. Recommended next action: label Priority: Low and mark ai-triage:done; maintainer-authored, precisely scoped, and has a full workaround, safe to label without further review.

title: OpenAI provider incorrectly maps params(top_k=) to top_logprobs
rationale: Facts: maintainer cpsievert self-filed this, showing that chatlas/_provider_openai.py maps the standardized top_k chat parameter directly onto OpenAI's unrelated top_logprobs field (if 'top_k' in params: res['top_logprobs'] = params['top_k']), so setting top_k silently changes the number of returned log-probabilities instead of affecting sampling, and vice versa; cites ellmer's just-merged equivalent fix (tidyverse/ellmer#1115, issue #1113) across its OpenAI-based providers, and suggests chatlas likely drop/warn on top_k for OpenAI-based providers rather than repurposing it, matching ellmer's resolution. Classification hypothesis: bug -- a parameter-mapping defect that silently corrupts unrelated response metadata. Duplicate check: searched 'top_k OR top_logprobs'; no other open duplicate found. Wrong-location check: correct repo -- chatlas/_provider_openai.py (and possibly _provider_openai_completions.py, flagged for the same check). Regression check: not applicable -- no evidence this mapping ever behaved differently in an older chatlas release. Reproduction plan: not included as a runnable script, but the defect is precisely located and self-evident from the cited source line; mirrors an already-merged upstream ellmer fix. Impact: moderate -- any user setting top_k against an OpenAI-based provider gets a silently wrong result (altered logprobs count instead of altered sampling), which could go unnoticed. Priority: Medium. Recommended next action: label Priority: Medium and mark ai-triage:done; maintainer-authored, precisely diagnosed, low-risk fix mirroring a shipped upstream change, safe to label without further review.

title: Add on_request_start() / on_request_end() hooks to Chat
rationale: Facts: maintainer cpsievert self-filed this feature request to add on_request_start()/on_request_end() hooks to Chat, mirroring ellmer's just-merged equivalent (tidyverse/ellmer#1052); unlike chatlas's existing tool-level callbacks (on_tool_request(), on_tool_result()), these would fire around each model request within the tool-calling loop (not just around individual tool calls), letting callers inspect/rewrite turns between tool rounds (e.g. to compact context); specifies the callback should work in both chat() and chat_async() paths. title: `ChatBedrock()` mantle APIs: default model isn't served, and cross-region prefix isn't stripped from requests
rationale: Facts: contributor thisisnic self-filed this (found while porting a related fix to ellmer), showing two related Bedrock-mantle-endpoint problems on the messages/responses APIs: (1) ChatBedrock(api='messages') with no explicit model defaults to DEFAULT_MODEL (us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6), which mantle's Anthropic endpoint does not serve, producing a live 404 in the included repro; (2) CROSS_REGION_PREFIX is stripped only for the internal MODEL_APIS lookup, not from the model id actually sent in the request, so a prefixed id that routes to mantle also 404s. Cites ellmer's fix (defaulting per-API and stripping the prefix from the request when the API is messages/responses via aws_strip_region_prefix()) as the template to mirror, and states this was tested against chatlas main (0.22.1.dev5). Classification hypothesis: bug -- two concrete, live-tested defects in Bedrock-mantle default-model selection and id normalization. Duplicate check: searched 'Bedrock'; found #415 (env-var base_url) and #410 (URL content sources) as distinct, unrelated Bedrock-mantle bugs from the same reporter, not duplicates of this default-model/prefix issue. Wrong-location check: correct repo -- chatlas' Bedrock provider implementation. Regression check: not applicable -- no evidence mantle ever served the current default model or accepted the prefixed id; appears to be a pre-existing gap surfaced while porting to ellmer. Reproduction plan: both sub-issues include exact runnable snippets against chatlas main with the literal resulting 404 error messages already captured. Impact: moderate -- breaks default (no-model-specified) usage of ChatBedrock(api='messages') against the mantle endpoint outright, and separately breaks any prefixed cross-region model id routed to mantle; scoped to users of that specific endpoint configuration rather than all Bedrock users. Priority: Medium. Recommended next action: label Priority: Medium and mark ai-triage:done; precisely diagnosed with live-tested repros and a clear fix template from ellmer, safe to label without further review.

title: `ChatBedrock()` mantle APIs send URL content sources, which Bedrock rejects
rationale: Facts: contributor thisisnic self-filed this (found while porting to ellmer), showing that content_pdf_url()/content_document_url() now pass the URL directly to the provider instead of sending bytes, and that BedrockMessagesProvider/BedrockResponsesProvider inherit this URL-passing behavior from AnthropicProvider/OpenAIProvider, but Bedrock's mantle endpoint cannot fetch external URLs, so both the Anthropic-style and OpenAI-style mantle paths return live 400 errors in the included repro (captured against chatlas main 0.22.1.dev5, anthropic 1.2.0, openai 3.6.0); notes content_image_url() fails the same way on both endpoints for an unrelated, pre-existing reason, and that local files work fine on both endpoints today. Points to ellmer's fix (override content serialization on the two mantle classes to drop the URL and fall back to already-fetched bytes) as the template. Classification hypothesis: bug -- a defect introduced by a prior URL-passing change (referenced as '#345'), not present for local-file content. Duplicate check: searched 'Bedrock'; distinct from #415 and #411 (different reporter-filed Bedrock-mantle bugs), no duplicate found. Wrong-location check: correct repo -- chatlas' Bedrock mantle provider classes. Regression check: no chatlas-release-vs-release comparison is given (the underlying limitation is Bedrock's own URL-fetch restriction being newly exposed by an internal serialization change, not an older chatlas release behaving differently), so not labeled regression per the rubric's evidence bar. Reproduction plan: the issue includes exact runnable snippets against chatlas main with the literal resulting 400 error messages already captured for both mantle paths. Impact: moderate -- breaks URL-based PDF/document content specifically on Bedrock's mantle endpoint; local-file content is unaffected, providing a workaround. Priority: Medium. Recommended next action: label Priority: Medium and mark ai-triage:done; precisely diagnosed with live-tested repros and a clear fix template from ellmer, safe to label without further review.

title: Databricks typed streaming content is serialized before normalization
rationale: Facts: community reporter srod-mckesson (self-disclosed as agent-assisted) reports that DatabricksProvider.stream_content() normalizes typed delta.content lists, but stream_merge_chunks() runs first and the inherited OpenAICompletionsProvider.stream_merge_chunks() calls chunk.model_dump() before that normalization happens; for a Databricks GPT-OSS chunk with list-valued delta.content, this both raises a PydanticSerializationUnexpectedValue warning and lets the unnormalized list enter generic accumulation, so a later normal string-content chunk gets merged character-by-character instead of appended as text. Cites related issue #392/PR #397 as handling the later stream_content() conversion but not this earlier merge-before-normalize ordering, and includes a standalone repro script constructing a typed reasoning chunk followed by a text chunk, showing both the corrupted character-split output and the serializer warning. Classification hypothesis: bug -- a chunk-processing order defect in Databricks streaming, narrower than and distinct from the already-fixed #392/#397. Duplicate check: found #392 (closed, 'fix(databricks): normalize typed GPT-OSS response content') as a related prior fix, but this issue targets a different, earlier point in the pipeline per the report's own explanation, so not a duplicate. Wrong-location check: correct repo -- chatlas/_provider_databricks.py. Regression check: not applicable -- no prior-release comparison; this is a gap left by a previous partial fix. Reproduction plan: the included standalone script (feeding a typed reasoning chunk then a text chunk through stream_merge_chunks() directly) is runnable and demonstrates both the corrupted content and the warning. Impact: low -- a narrow edge case specific to Databricks GPT-OSS models emitting typed reasoning content mixed with later plain-text chunks during streaming. Priority: Low. Recommended next action: label Priority: Low and mark ai-triage:done; well-specified with a runnable repro and a precise fix location, though the report is agent-assisted and unverified by a maintainer -- safe to label as a low-priority, low-risk fix candidate rather than treating as urgent.

title: Per-turn context cannot be attached to a message sent by `chat_server()`
rationale: Facts: community contributor nbenn reports that chat_server() gives an app no way to attach extra content (e.g. RAG-retrieved excerpts, or a snapshot of app/document state) to the message it sends, because the module reads the input value and calls stream_async() directly, and there is no way to intercept it from outside: ellmer::Chat is unexported (cannot subclass), its instances are binding-locked, and the returned module environment is lockEnvironment()-sealed. Explains in detail why rewriting the system prompt is not a substitute (it retroactively replaces context for the whole prior transcript, breaks prompt-caching cost, and confuses RAG per-question evidence with standing instructions), and why this is not a repeat of previously-closed #10 (that issue's 'own the observer' workaround assumed direct access to stream_async(), which the newer chat_server() module (#264) now owns internally). Proposes a concrete on_submit() callback API mirroring the existing mod$history$on_save() pattern, and offers to open a PR. Classification hypothesis: feature -- a well-reasoned, well-scoped API gap in a newer module, explicitly distinguished from the prior closed issue it might otherwise appear to duplicate. Duplicate check: found closed #10 ('input and response transforms') -- the issue itself explains why it is not a duplicate; no open duplicate found. Wrong-location check: correct repo -- shinychat's R chat_server() module. Regression check: not applicable -- this is a missing capability in newer code (chat_server(), #264), not a behavior change from an older release. Reproduction plan: not applicable to a feature request; the issue traces the exact code path (pkg-r/R/chat_app.R#L427) and the specific access barriers (unexported class, locked bindings, sealed environment) that block a workaround today. Impact: moderate -- blocks two concrete, common use cases (RAG apps, stateful/editable-document apps) from working correctly with chat_server(), with no viable workaround given the sealed module internals. Priority: Medium. Recommended next action: label Priority: Medium and mark ai-triage:done; thorough, well-scoped community proposal with no viable workaround today, safe to label without further review.

title: Chat messages mixing markdown strings and HTML tags no longer render strings as markdown
rationale: Facts: maintainer cpsievert self-filed this, showing that a chat message mixing markdown-formatted strings and HTML tags (e.g. a TagList with a string and a div) no longer renders the string portion as markdown -- it appears as literal text (**bold** instead of bold) -- contradicting the documented append_message()/chat_append() behavior ('strings are still interpreted as markdown as long as they're not inside HTML'); affects both append_message()/append_message_stream() (Python) and chat_append()/chat_append_stream() (R). Includes a runnable Python repro against Chat.append_message() with a TagList. Provides an explicit regression table verified by running the same example in a browser against old commits: behavior rendered strings as markdown before Sep 2025, and stopped after commit 02ce6bf0 (#119, Sep 2025, which wrapped HTML content in a 'raw HTML' code block to display it as-is) -- an unintended side effect of #119 rather than its goal -- and remained broken through the #181 Lit-to-React UI rewrite and the #208 explicit-content-type change. Diagnoses the root cause as an all-or-nothing per-message content-type decision, and proposes a per-piece fix building on open PR #360's per-piece logic, noting the wire format already supports multiple segments per message. Classification hypothesis: regression -- current behavior materially differs from pre-Sep-2025 behavior, with commit-level evidence and root-cause diagnosis. Duplicate check: searched 'markdown HTML TagList'; no duplicate found (only itself and an unrelated Pydantic-AI feature request, #169). Wrong-location check: correct repo -- shinychat's shared chat-message rendering logic (Python and R packages both affected). Regression check: evidence cited -- a commit-by-commit table (pre-Sep-2025 working, broken starting at 02ce6bf0/#119, still broken through #181 and #208) satisfies the rubric's regression bar. Reproduction plan: the included Python TagList repro against Chat.append_message() is directly runnable and matches the documented-vs-actual behavior described. Impact: moderate-to-high -- silently breaks a documented capability across both language packages, specifically affecting patterns like RAG apps or dashboards that combine model-generated markdown text with server-rendered widgets in one message; a partial fix foundation (PR #360) is already in flight. Priority: High -- high-confidence, well-evidenced regression per the priority guide. Recommended next action: label Priority: High and regression, and mark ai-triage:done; maintainer-authored with commit-level regression evidence, root cause, and an in-progress fix foundation, safe to label without further review.
